result.summary: The image depicts a high-speed roadway environment characterized by a large sound wall and a complete absence of pedestrian infrastructure. There are no sidewalks, crosswalks, or streetlights, making the area extremely hostile and unsafe for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Facilities
hazards.description: There is no sidewalk or paved path, forcing any pedestrians to walk on the grass verge or the roadway shoulder.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway along the sound wall

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Wide travel lanes and the presence of a sound wall indicate a high-speed arterial or highway environment with no protection for people outside of vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Street Lighting
hazards.description: No luminaires are visible, which would make pedestrians nearly invisible to drivers at night.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a paved sidewalk separated from the roadway by a buffer to provide a safe space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for all road users during nighttime hours.

interventions.title: Physical Separation
interventions.description: If this is a high-speed corridor, install a physical barrier or significant green buffer between the roadway and any future pedestrian path.

result.summary: The environment is highly hostile to pedestrians, characterized by a complete absence of sidewalks and marked crossings. The wide roadway with dashed lane markings suggests a high-speed vehicular environment with no physical separation or protection for people walking.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Facilities
hazards.description: There are no sidewalks or designated walking paths, forcing pedestrians to walk in the grass or on the high-speed roadway.

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Wide lanes and dashed markings without traffic calming measures encourage high vehicle speeds in an area with no pedestrian protection.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a paved sidewalk separated from the roadway to provide a safe, dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility for all road users, especially if pedestrians are expected to use the area at night.

interventions.title: Marked Crossings
interventions.description: If pedestrian demand exists, install high-visibility marked crosswalks with appropriate signage and potentially signalization.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is highly hostile, characterized by a complete lack of sidewalks and marked crossings on a wide roadway. Pedestrians are forced to share space with vehicular traffic without any physical separation or designated crossing points in a residential context.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: No paved walkway exists for pedestrians, forcing them onto the grass or the roadway shoulder in close proximity to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both sides of the main roadway throughout the frame.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: The intersection lacks marked crosswalks, providing no designated or protected space for pedestrians to cross the wide road.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct continuous paved sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide physical separation between pedestrians and vehicles.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility marked crosswalks and pedestrian crossing warning signs at the intersection to define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to reduce the crossing distance and improve the visibility of pedestrians to drivers.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with basic pedestrian infrastructure, including sidewalks and a stop-controlled approach. While some crosswalk markings are visible, they appear faded, and the wide intersection geometry increases exposure for pedestrians crossing the street.

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The existing crosswalk markings on the right side of the intersection are faded, reducing their visibility to approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the intersection crossing the side street.

hazards.name: Wide Intersection Geometry
hazards.description: The wide turning radii and lack of curb extensions increase the distance pedestrians must travel in the roadway, increasing exposure time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade existing faded markings to high-visibility continental or ladder style crosswalks on all legs of the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) to shorten crossing distances, improve sightlines, and slow down turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add lighting specifically oriented toward the sidewalk and crossing areas to improve nighttime visibility.
